Subject: Annual token commit proposal for Peakify — summary attached

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for taking the call yesterday — excited to keep momentum. Per our conversation I attached a short one-page proposal with three annual commit tiers tailored to Peakify's usage forecast and ramp profile. High-level summary below: 

- Starter: 100M tokens/year — 15% off hosted per-token list price (recommended for pilot and initial production apps)
- Growth: 500M tokens/year — 27% off list price (for teams scaling multi-product usage)
- Enterprise: 2B tokens/year — 40% off list price + SLA & dedicated support channel

Example: assumed list price $0.00060/token -> Starter effective $0.00051/token, Growth $0.000438/token, Enterprise $0.00036/token. We include quarterly reconciliation and the ability to map commits to up to 5 API projects. Overage usage billed at 10% above the committed unit price; unused committed volume can be rolled forward up to one quarter (calendar) on a case-by-case basis.

Attachments: redwood-peakify-commit-proposal.pdf (proposal one-pager), mutual-action-plan.docx (MAM draft).

Questions I anticipated: monthly ramp flexibility, attribution of commits to API keys, and whether commit can convert to Dedicated later. I added short notes on each in the attached. If this looks good I'd like to lock a draft and get the RevOps team into a quick call to align on billing cadence and signature.

Would Thursday or Friday afternoon work for a 30-min alignment?

Best,
Ben

Ben,

Thanks — this is helpful. A few clarifying questions from our side before we schedule a sign-off call: 

1) Ramp and monthly burn: Peakify expects a 3-month ramp (20% / 40% / 40% of annual forecast). Can we front-load credits or reflect a monthly true-up rather than forcing even monthly commitments?
2) Overage and refunds: if we exceed the commit in Q1 but come in under for the full year, how are overages reconciled?
3) Attribution: we want the ability to allocate committed tokens to specific product API keys and projects — is that standard or a custom mapping?
4) Contract conversion: if we later move to Dedicated, can we port unused committed dollars/tokens to a Dedicated reservation?

Also: can you share a simple scenario comparing total annual cost for Growth vs Enterprise for a 600M token year? Our CFO will want that calc.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Avery Smith <avery@peakify.com>
Cc: Peakify RevOps <revops@peakify.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-24T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Annual token commit proposal for Peakify — clarifications + scenario

Avery — great questions. Short answers up front, then a worked example.

1) Ramp/flex: Yes — we support monthly true-ups tied to the annual commit. You can overconsume early; we'll reconcile quarterly. If consumption is materially above the forecast long-term (>30% difference) we will engage to adjust the next quarter's allocations.
2) Overage/refund: Overage billed at +10% of the committed unit price during the quarter. If by year-end committed volume exceeds consumed tokens, we allow a one-quarter rollover of unused tokens; beyond that we credit unused tokens at 50% of the committed unit price applied to future invoices (standard practice for hosted commit agreements).
3) Attribution: We can map a commit across named API keys/projects at contract execution (up to 10 distinct keys). That mapping is editable with 30 days notice to support internal billing splits.
4) Conversion to Dedicated: We can convert remaining committed value to a Dedicated reservation credit; conversion requires 60 days notice and a short migration addendum. Any upfront discounts that applied to the hosted commit will be reconciled on conversion (we apply the greater of the committed credit or the Dedicated effective value).

Worked example (Growth vs Enterprise) for 600M tokens/year (assume list $0.00060/token):
- Growth (500M commit at 27% discount): committed unit price = $0.000438; commit cost = 500M * $0.000438 = $219,000; overage price = $0.000438 * 1.10 = $0.0004818. For 600M actual usage -> year cost = commit cost + (100M * overage price) = $219,000 + $48,180 = $267,180.
- Enterprise (2B commit at 40% discount): committed unit price = $0.00036; commit cost (if you kept 2B) = $720,000 (but you would likely not choose a 2B if you only need 600M). If we structure a 600M effective Enterprise-like arrangement (annualized pricing at Enterprise rates pro-rated), 600M * $0.00036 = $216,000.

So for 600M, the Enterprise effective spend (at Enterprise unit price) would be ~ $216k vs Growth ramp scenario at ~$267k (per above). The math shows Enterprise unit pricing beats Growth once you secure the Enterprise unit price; the Enterprise tier is designed for customers who intend sustained multi-product usage.

Options I can propose: 
- Option A (Short-term): Sign Growth at 500M with monthly true-ups (you pay overage for month > allocation).
- Option B (Aggressive savings): Sign Enterprise at 2B for 40% off (requires exec OK) — big savings per token but higher upfront commitment.
- Option C (Middle path): 600M custom commit at 35% off (custom discount), annualized — this yields unit price $0.00039 total cost $234k and is convertible to Dedicated under the standard addendum. Requires Sales + RevOps approval.

Attached: pricing-scenarios.csv (per-month breakdown), mutual-action-plan.docx (draft MAM).

If you want, I can put this into a short two-slide decision memo for your CFO showing cashflow and the break-even month between Option A and C. I can do that before our Friday call.

Best,
Ben
